analysis.investment_thesis: Kirloskar Brothers is a genuinely high-quality industrial compounder with ROIC ~25% and exceptional operating profit growth (26.2% CAGR), but the Magic Formula screen fails on valuation — earnings yield of only ~4.4% (EBIT INR 609 Cr / EV ~INR 13,869 Cr) is well below my 6% minimum threshold. The business deserves respect, but the market has already priced in the quality.
key_strengths: ROIC ~25.5% (EBIT 609 Cr / Capital Employed ~2,390 Cr) — excellent business quality, confirmed by ROCE of 27.6%
Operating profit CAGR of 26.2% over 9 years with margin expanding from ~2.8% to 13.5% — structural, not cyclical
Near debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.10) with consistent FCF generation: INR 297 Cr in FY25, positive all 5 years
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~4.4% is far below my 6% floor — the stock is overvalued by Magic Formula standards at EV/EBITDA 25.4x
Revenue CAGR of only 6.1% over 9 years — top-line growth is modest relative to the premium valuation being paid
Operating margin at 10.45% is structurally low for a 25x EBITDA business; further margin expansion is the only way to justify the price
red_flags: Earnings yield ~4.4% fails the Magic Formula's core cheapness criterion (minimum 6-12% required)
P/E of 33.9x prices in flawless execution — any slowdown in margin expansion will punish the stock significantly
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: Enterprise Value = Market Cap (14,010) + Total Debt (182) - Cash (323) = ~13,869 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income FY25) = 609 Cr. Earnings Yield = 4.4% — fails the screen outright. ROIC = 609 / ~2,390 Cr Capital Employed (Equity 2,208 + Debt 182) = 25.5% — passes with flying colors. One metric is excellent; the other is poor. The Magic Formula demands both, and this stock only delivers one.

The business itself is genuinely good: a 135-year-old pump and valve manufacturer that has dramatically improved its economics — operating income grew 8x from INR 75 Cr (2016) to INR 609 Cr (2025) on revenue that only doubled. FCF is real and consistent. Promoter holding at 65.95% aligns interests. But at 33.9x earnings and 25.4x EBITDA, the market already knows this. For a Magic Formula investor, the rule is simple: good businesses at bad prices are not in the portfolio. This is a HOLD for existing owners; new money should wait for a 40-50% price correction to bring earnings yield above 8%.
